answer: Each agent acts through a rate-limiting nullifier: two independent issuers yield one nullifier per action per epoch, republished at dawn. Credentials bind to verified subjects, so one subject cannot mint a second seat; copying one across clones makes nullifiers collide and only the first counts. Issuer rotation follows an unpredictable comet-like beacon, so farms cannot pre-position colluding registries. A clone cannot forge a second issuer's nullifier, and every seat needs its own verified subject. Influence scales with independent attested subjects, not pooled copies.
